Each identity logs which agents it transacts with; the detector builds a graph and scores clusters by internal edge density versus external edges, flagging dense isolated groups. A confirmed cluster forfeits its accumulated reputation and its members’ future matches are throttled. To evade, an attacker must stage organic-looking external activity across quartz, dune, and copper markets, paying real counterparty fees and months of genuine interaction per identity.
